units: lux on an unobstructed horizontal surface
evidence: Scalar spherical multiple scattering on the solved 1.2-atm column; finite sources integrated over a point-source response.
reading_rule: Linear interpolation in native source-elevation nodes and phase. Disk integration follows evaluator.mjs. No stellar/airglow floor is added.

atmosphere.geometry: Spherical, horizontally uniform molecular column; straight rays

source_model.earth_spectrum: Glenar et al. 2019; visual normalization Robinson et al. 2025
source_model.phase_bounds: Spectral fit derived below 60 degrees and extrapolated; spectral shape held beyond 144 degrees. Visual observations span 5 to 144 degrees; a continuous Lambert-shaped tail reaches new Earth.
source_model.disk: Lambert incidence pattern normalized to measured disk-integrated phase brightness; spatial spectrum uniform
source_model.finite_distance: Topocentric directions, angular radii and distances; the atmosphere response to each disk element uses parallel rays
source_model.variation: Mean Earth spectrum; continents, seasons and cloud changes are not predicted

spectrum.reading_rule: Band-integrated flux at 1 AU solar distance and the reference Earth/Moon distance. Apparent disk reflectance is Earth irradiance divided by incident solar band irradiance and (Earth radius/reference distance)^2; phase zero is the geometric-albedo spectrum.

sources.title: Glenar et al., Earthshine as an illumination source at the Moon
Robinson et al. (2025), Earth phase curve
